# memory

```go
import "github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
```

Package memory is a gashe.Backend that lives in the memory of this process: a fixed\-size LRU with per\-entry TTL. Other processes do not see its entries.

## type [Backend](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/backend/memory/memory.go#L46-L56>)

Backend is an in\-process gashe.Backend. Create it with New and stop it with Close.

```go
type Backend struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/backend/memory/memory.go#L68>)

```go
func New(o Options) *Backend
```

New returns a memory Backend and starts its background purge. It panics on a negative MaxEntries or MaxBytes.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{MaxEntries: 2})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	for _, key := range []string{"a", "b", "c"} {
		_ = c.Set(ctx, key, 1, 0)
	}
	a, _ := c.Exists(ctx, "a") // the least recently used entry was evicted
	fmt.Println(mem.Len(), a)
}
```

#### Output

```
2 false
```

</p>

<a name="Options"></a>
## type [Options](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/backend/memory/memory.go#L31-L43>)

Options configures a memory Backend. The zero value is ready to use.

```go
type Options struct {
    // MaxEntries is the maximum number of entries, not bytes; the least recently used one is
    // evicted when it is exceeded. 0 means 1000.
    MaxEntries int
    // MaxBytes is the most bytes keys and values may take together; the least recently used
    // entries are evicted to stay under it. It counts the bytes of keys and values only, not the
    // overhead of the Go runtime, so leave headroom. 0 means no limit.
    MaxBytes int64
    // PurgeInterval is how often expired entries are purged in the background.
    // 0 means one second; a negative value turns the purge off. Expired entries are never
    // returned either way.
    PurgeInterval time.Duration
}
```
